nodes.label: Daily clean-up cron (/api/cron/daily)
nodes.rationale: Besides deleting unsent uploads, expired sessions and old sign-in counters, its daily query stops the free Supabase project from pausing after a week with no use.

nodes.label: Nightly backup (npm run backup)
nodes.rationale: Supabase's free plan has no backups, so the QA laptop's copy is the only one. It holds ticket data and must stay on the laptop or an office drive.

nodes.label: Task Scheduler job QA Hub backup

nodes.label: Lighter on the free plan
nodes.rationale: About 945 MB of downloads in one day, mostly one video reloaded on every visit, against a 5 GB monthly allowance; so videos load on Play, screenshots become WebP and files are reused for 5 minutes.

nodes.label: Database change workflow
nodes.rationale: Migrations are applied before pushing code so the live site never runs against a database that lacks the change.

nodes.label: Egress reduction measures
nodes.rationale: Videos load only on Play, the browser reuses a file for 5 minutes, and screenshots are saved as WebP before upload, to stay inside the 5 GB monthly egress limit.

nodes.label: RLS on with no policies
nodes.rationale: Supabase's public API with the publishable key can read nothing; only QA Hub's server with the secret key reaches the data.

nodes.label: Device notifications (web push)
nodes.rationale: The server only accepts push addresses of the real browser push services, so nobody can make it call another URL.

nodes.label: Install as an app (Phase 3.7c)
nodes.rationale: Keeps no copy of pages or tickets, so offline shows the browser's normal no-connection page and no ticket data sits on the device.

nodes.label: New ticket drafts
nodes.rationale: Switching apps to take more screenshots on a phone must lose nothing; unusable after 24 hours.

nodes.label: Installing QA Hub as an app
nodes.norm_label: installing qa hub as an app
nodes.rationale: The app keeps no pages or tickets on the device, so with no connection it shows the browser's normal offline page.

nodes.label: Show message previews setting
nodes.rationale: Previews show ticket titles and messages, which can expose customer names and amounts on screens, so each person can turn them off and should hide them while the device is locked.

nodes.label: Ticket data is sensitive, never sent to AI

nodes.rationale: A mistaken move can be taken back on the same ticket instead of filing a new one; a required note tells the other side why.

nodes.label: dcwd_apps-csms-bca-api
nodes.rationale: .NET 8 modular monolith. Its consistent pattern: validate a command, guard its stage or sequence, persist the record and audit entry together, then let queues and workers reconcile and notify.

nodes.label: Quartz Background Jobs
nodes.rationale: Single-process scheduler risk: jobs run in the API process, so scaling without a cluster-safe lock risks duplicate execution and recycling the host interrupts work.

nodes.label: Nightly Seeding Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Meter reading, rate, meter-rate and legacy meter-change imports stay manual because the user supplies the file or rate context.

nodes.label: NSC Authorization Risk
nodes.rationale: Key NSC staff and admin actions have historically relied on authenticated-user access or UI gating rather than complete server-side policy enforcement.

nodes.label: Phase 3.5 QA Ticket Hub
nodes.rationale: QA and developers stop using Messenger for bugs; replaces the planned Phase 9 Defects screen.

nodes.label: Phase 3.6a Test Library and Manual Runs
nodes.norm_label: phase 3.6a test library and manual runs
nodes.rationale: Comes first because Phase B automates the cases Phase A writes down.

nodes.label: Phase 3.7 QA Hub on Phones
nodes.rationale: Testers should file a bug on the same phone right after it happens, instead of sending the screenshot to a laptop first.

nodes.label: Phase 3.7a Mobile UI Rework
nodes.rationale: On hold since 2026-11-03 because redesigns were not accepted; the user is designing the UI in the Claude Design canvas first.

nodes.label: Phase 9 Controls Suite and Quality Gate
nodes.norm_label: phase 9 controls suite and quality gate
nodes.rationale: COA findings on utility billing focus on internal controls, so the suite covers segregation of duties, approval enforcement, audit trail, tariff tables and OR integrity.

nodes.label: QA AI for In-House ERP Build Plan
nodes.norm_label: qa ai for in-house erp build plan
nodes.rationale: Roadmap for QA Hub. Sections 1-7 and Phases 4-11 are the original workbench design, kept as background for Phase 3.6; CLAUDE.md wins where they conflict.

nodes.label: Hybrid Privacy Routing
nodes.rationale: Original workbench rule: sensitive data goes local only or is redacted before a cloud call, and sensitive tasks fail rather than fall back to the cloud. The lib/ai code has since been removed.

nodes.label: Phase 6 Business-Process Suites
nodes.rationale: ERP failures happen between modules, so coverage is measured by business journey with assertions at each hand-off, not by screen count.

nodes.label: Deterministic Oracles
nodes.rationale: Money, quantities and balances are checked by code, never AI opinion. LLM oracles are not a source of truth; accounting or billing sign-off on hand-worked examples is the trust anchor.

nodes.label: Sign-up approval
nodes.rationale: The sign-in page is on the internet, so admin approval is the gate; approved users can see every ticket.

nodes.label: MCR Control Flow
nodes.rationale: Approval does not alter the customer record; only posting does. Posting re-runs readiness checks because payment, meter, contract or assignment conditions can change after approval.

nodes.label: Additive migration first, code second
nodes.rationale: The live site never misses a column while code and schema deploy separately.
